//: The cross-half contract index -- M2 of docs/design/CONTRACTS_DEDUPE_PLAN.md, and the answer to
the ninth audit's I-13 ('two Phase-10 boxes are closable by a Builder change').
WHAT THIS DIRECTORY IS. contracts/ is the SOURCE of every schema listed below. The copy under
engine/schemas/ is a vendored artifact held byte-identical by tools/check_contracts_single_source.py:
edit the copy alone and CI goes RED naming the file. That is the property the roadmap box asks
for -- one definition both halves are held to -- obtained WITHOUT changing how the engine loads
schemas.
WHY THE ENGINE STILL READS ITS OWN COPY, stated so nobody 'finishes' the job by deleting it.
The engine resolves every schema path relative to its OWN root (engine/schemas/registry.json
holds root-relative paths; bro_contracts.validate_registered_schemas and bro_orchestration read
them that way). Pointing those loaders at ../contracts/ makes the engine read outside its root,
which is a deliberate change to the containment model its perimeter is built on -- and engine/ is
a git subtree of menqstudio/Bro, so moving files out of it forks the vendored half from upstream.
That relocation is M2's remaining step and it needs its own audited engine branch. It is NOT
blocked by the production gate, by any service principal, launcher, broker or deployment, and
this file exists so the box is not filed under a blocker it never had.
VERSIONING. version_pointer is a JSON Pointer into the schema itself, resolved by the gate and
compared with `version`. Four of the five carry `schema: {const: 1}` at the top level; mode-grant
is a signed envelope, so its version lives at payload.schema. A bump has to be made in the schema
AND here, in one commit, or the gate reports the disagreement.

contracts.why_shared: the lease is what the wall issues and the cockpit displays; both halves read the same object
contracts.rust_mirror_note: NONE, and that is the fact rather than a gap to fill. No Rust file in this tree mirrors the execution lease: `grep -rln 'execution-lease.schema|struct ExecutionLease' --include=*.rs apps/desktop/src-tauri/` returns nothing, and check_schema_mirrors.py's MIRRORS table carries only VerifierReceipt and EvidenceEvent. This field named core/src/governance.rs, a path that has never existed; pointing it at the real governance.rs would have replaced a dead path with a false claim.

contracts.why_shared: the signed envelope that raises a session's mode; the desktop shows its state and never mints one
the desktop drafts it (agentsDispatch) and the engine is the only party that accepts it
the only artifact that can make the desktop say Verified; it is parsed on the desktop side
the append-only chain the security page mirrors; the desktop reads it and appends nothing

the first contract that crosses in THIS direction: the cockpit asks and the engine records. Both halves have to agree on what an ask is allowed to contain, and the answer is enforced structurally -- additionalProperties false, with no key, signature, nonce, lease or verdict field in it at all
contracts.rust_mirror_note: NONE yet, and deliberately: the desktop command that sends this document does not exist. T-021 is three steps -- this schema audited before it lands, then the engine endpoint, then the Tauri command -- because docs/OWNER_ACTION_REQUIRED.md fixed five contract invariants and the fifth is that the engine schema change is audited BEFORE the transport that carries it. A Rust mirror added here would be a mirror of a message nothing sends. It arrives with the command, and check_schema_mirrors.py's table is where it will be declared

engine_internal.//: The other 15 schemas in engine/schemas/ are consumed by the engine alone. Moving them buys churn, not a binding -- CONTRACTS_DEDUPE_PLAN.md M2. Listed so the gate can assert the split is exhaustive rather than assumed.

desktop_internal.//: Schemas consumed by the desktop half alone, living beside the code that owns them at apps/desktop/src-tauri/core/schema/. They are NOT contracts: nothing in engine/ reads them, so every entry above carries `crosses` and these carry none. Listed so tools/check_contracts_single_source.py can assert the split is exhaustive rather than assumed -- the same reason engine_internal exists.

wire_protocols_that_stay_put.//: M3 of the plan, recorded as a decision so a later reader does not fold them in: these are protocols between two NAMED processes, not shared domain objects, and they are correctly filed next to the process that serves them.
